text: Implement the native openvela Ethernet candidate described in /mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/function-ethernet-e404/task.txt. Read that file directly, then s31-reference/AGENTS.md and the listed driver sources; no broad searches through backups. Work only in this candidate directory, with no hardware access. Root identified Function MAC 30:ed:a0:f3:f7:b0,16MiB, UARTworking and original backupreading. Prior independentCLI attempts ended due stream disconnect without implementation; no safety rejection. Produce actual native driver/profile/build. Keep all edits private because maintained source is being packaged. Report architecture/pins first, then complete implementation.

I’ll read the task file, then the candidate’s instructions and listed sources. I’ll report the architecture and pin mapping before implementing and building, with all work confined to the candidate directory and no hardware access.

The locked HAL has the S31 RGMII MAC/DMA code and a generic gigabit PHY driver. The IDF example also documents the required YT8531 autonegotiation and clock-delay setup. I’m checking the Function board pin references and the NuttX OS adapter before choosing how much of that HAL path to reuse.

I’ll implement a native NuttX `eth0` using the locked HAL’s MAC/DMA and PHY code, with NuttX deferred work and locking. The HAL’s RX task notifications are not ported, so I’ll replace that scheduling path in the private candidate.

The pin mapping is MDC 5, MDIO 6, reset 7; TXD0–3 8–11, TX_CTL 12, TX_CLK 13; RX_CLK 14, RX_CTL 15, RXD0–3 19/18/17/16. This follows the local IDF defaults and Espressif’s documented RGMII group A. I’ll use PHY address discovery and the example’s approximately 2 ns RX/TX delays. [Official pin guide](https://esp32-s31.espressif.com/en/docs/6-Pinout%20%26%20IO%20%E8%B5%84%E6%BA%90/%E5%A4%96%E8%AE%BE%E7%AE%A1%E8%84%9A%E5%88%86%E9%85%8D%E8%AF%B4%E6%98%8E)

The private profile and HAL adaptations are in place. I also found a clock-selection issue: the HAL’s automatic path tries MPLL first and can fail because its 20 MHz steps cannot produce the required 125 MHz RGMII clock. The candidate explicitly selects APLL. I’m now adding packet ownership, link handling and TX retry before building.

The native driver is written, including bounded RX processing, queued TX retry, PHY identity checks, link updates and interface down/up handling. The offline environment check passed, and the first clean build is configuring. I’ve also corrected the profile to use this openvela version’s `NETINIT_*` static-address settings.

The first configure attempt exposed two build-isolation issues: the host compiler wrapper tried to use a cache outside the candidate, and the HAL’s relative Git metadata path broke in the shadow tree. Both are fixed locally. The next clean build is progressing; I’m checking DMA ordering and TX backpressure while it runs.

The host checks passed for TX backpressure, buffer reuse, failed DMA-stop handling, link-state reporting and PHY register guards. Compilation is underway.

I also found an existing build rule that touched the maintained `lib_utsname.c` timestamp despite source-preservation mode. Its contents are unchanged. I’m disabling that rule in the candidate profile so subsequent builds keep that operation private.

The three adapted HAL sources pass syntax checks with the locked RISC-V compiler. The native driver check found one header-path mismatch, which I’ve corrected. I’ve started a fresh full build with the timestamp rule disabled and faster lookup of shared headers; the host packet-ownership checks remain green.

The final native source now also handles stack-allocation failures without retransmitting the incoming frame. The PHY identity guard accepts the documented YT8531 and YT8531S variants while rejecting other IDs. Configuration has completed with the locked compiler, and the full build is generating its rules; board link and traffic results remain untested.

The full compile exposed another HAL gap: its general OS adapter depends on newer IRQ/task APIs that this openvela tree does not provide. I’m switching Ethernet IRQ setup directly to the existing NuttX allocator and retaining the minimal S31 OS adapter. That keeps Ethernet’s interrupt and scheduler ownership within NuttX.
The NuttX IRQ adaptation now compiles. The remaining failure is a missing header in the generic PHY source; I’ll fix that in the private overlay and continue the full build.

The driver now includes PHY identity checks, RGMII delay setup, link polling, bounded RX processing, and TX retry handling. The host checks pass for packet ownership, failed-stop recovery, carrier state, and PHY register guards. The full build is progressing; board boot and traffic tests remain for Root.

Compilation has passed the Ethernet sources and reached the NuttX libraries. The generated configuration confirms FLAT, one CPU, no Wi‑Fi or PSRAM, and `192.168.88.2/24`. After linking succeeds, I’ll run the required clean build and record the final hashes and handover commands.

The full build linked successfully and produced the ESP32-S31 simple-boot image for offset `0x2000`. I’m now running the required clean build, then checking the ELF, configuration, source hashes, and final handover report.

The ELF check caught a profile issue: `NETUTILS_PING` enables the library, but this tree requires `SYSTEM_PING` for the shell command. I’m correcting that and starting a fresh build. I’ll also remove the unsupported `SYSTEM_NETSTAT` option; interface statistics are available through `ifconfig`.

The fresh profile includes both `ping` and `iperf`, and all 21 offline dependency checks pass. A final DMA review found one recovery edge case: after a failed link-down stop, link-up could reset the ring while DMA was still active. I’m requiring a successful stop before every MAC start.

The new ownership check passes: a failed DMA stop prevents both descriptor reset and engine start. The corrected profile is compiling. The handover will include a bounded TCP/UDP peer script for Root; it has not been run or opened any sockets here.

The final clean rebuild is running with the ping fix and DMA recovery guard. Once it links, I’ll verify that the ELF includes the native driver, NuttX IRQ handler, `ping`, `iperf`, and interface commands, and that its sources match all 13 candidate files.

The clean build succeeded. The audit found that CMake had not applied the driver’s requested `-Werror` flag because the source property was set in the wrong scope. I’ve corrected it using this tree’s existing pattern and am rebuilding so the recorded compiler command enforces the intended check.

The native driver has now compiled with `-Wall -Werror`, and the clean build has no compile errors. I’m finishing the ELF and hash checks and writing the handover report, including the earlier timestamp-only touch and the board tests still pending.

Implemented the native S31/YT8531 Ethernet driver and Function-only FLAT profile. Clean full build, fault checks, ELF inspection, and hashes pass.

No hardware access or publication occurred. Board acceptance remains pending. Source contents stayed private; one early timestamp-only touch to maintained source is documented.
